cards.text: The prophet Zephaniah has been bringing the LORD's words (Zephaniah 1:1), and the last ones were heavy: the LORD will pour out His burning anger on nations and kingdoms, and all the earth will be consumed by the fire of His jealousy (Zephaniah 3:8). Then the LORD keeps going, friend, and the very next words out of His mouth are "For then."

cards.question: For then, the LORD says, He'll restore something to the peoples so all may call upon His name. What does He restore?

cards.text: All of them, serving the LORD "shoulder to shoulder." I spent YEARS shoulder to shoulder with dead batteries in a junk drawer, and all we ever did was argue about who had the most charge left.

cards.question: The LORD says His scattered worshipers are too far away, beyond the rivers of Cush, to ever bring Him an offering.

cards.text: Now the LORD turns to His own people and all the wrongs they've done against Him. Friend, if that were me, I'd be sweating right through my apron.

cards.question: On that day, the LORD says His people will still be put to shame for every wrong they did against Him.
The LORD will remove from among His people those who rejoice in their ___. And never again will they be haughty on His holy mountain.
With the proud removed, who does the LORD say He'll leave within His people?
That meek and humble people will ___ in the name of the LORD.

cards.text: The remnant of Israel won't do wrong or speak lies, and no deceitful tongue will be found in their mouths. Not even "I'm five minutes away" when you haven't found your keys yet.

cards.question: With no one to make them tremble, what will the remnant of Israel do?

cards.text: Then comes a call, and it is LOUD: sing for joy, shout aloud, be glad and rejoice with all your heart, Daughter of Jerusalem! That's me when a batch comes out of the oven perfect, except I live alone, so mostly I'm just yelling at a cookie.

cards.question: Why all the joy? The call says the LORD has taken something away from His people. What is it?

cards.text: And He has turned back your enemy. Turned them right around, like a bouncer who checks the list, looks back up, and just points at the parking lot.

cards.question: The call says Israel's King, the LORD, is among His people, and they will no longer fear any harm.

cards.text: On that day, they'll say to Jerusalem: "Do not fear, O Zion; do not let your hands fall limp." That's the exact opposite of your boss texting "got a minute?" and every bone in your body quitting at once.

cards.question: On that day, what reason will Zion be given not to fear?

answers.text: The LORD is among you and mighty to save
Your walls are rebuilt and standing strong
Your army is gathered and ready for battle

cards.text: It gets better, friend: He will rejoice over you with gladness, and He will rejoice over you with singing. I sing over my cookies, and honestly, the cookies have asked me to stop.

cards.question: Along with rejoicing over them, the LORD will ___ His people with His love.
The LORD speaks again, promising His people they will no longer suffer reproach. Who among them does He say He'll gather?

answers.text: Those who grieve over the appointed feasts
Those who rejoice in their pride
Those who rule over the nations

cards.text: Then the LORD says, "Behold, at that time, I will deal with all who afflict you." ALL of them, friend, and nobody slips out the back door.

cards.question: At that time, the LORD will save the ___ and gather the ___.
The LORD says the disgraced will stay hidden in their shame, far from the rest of the earth.

cards.text: "At that time I will bring you in; yes, at that time I will gather you." Friend, after years in the back of a junk drawer, I can tell you there are no sweeter words than hearing the LORD say He'll bring you in.

cards.question: When the LORD restores His people's captives before their very eyes, among whom will He give them fame and praise?

answers.text: All the peoples of the earth

findings.problem: The opening card identifies Zephaniah and the LORD and gives the judgment context, but it never says to whom Zephaniah is bringing the LORD's words.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The quotation begins with "I" before the speaker is named. The LORD is identified only in the sentence after the quotation; He should be named before it.

rule.text: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.
